document.title: Andropov-Gromyko-Ustinov-Ponomarev Report to CC CPSU on the Situation in Afghanistan, June 28, 1979
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Report to the Central Committee on the situation in Afghanistan. Source: CWIHP Bulletin 8-9, pp. 152-153. Together with Docs 5-6, it shows Soviet thinking on the wider geostrategic implications, the Iranian revolution, perceived U.S. goals, and suspected Amin-American cooperation.

events.description: Report submitted to the CC CPSU, and its recommendations approved at the Politburo meeting (Resolution P 156/XI): send an experienced general and officers, a parachute battalion to Bagram, a KGB detachment to Kabul, and a GRU detachment to Bagram.
actors: Communist Party of the Soviet Union

events.description: Planned dispatch of a GRU special detachment to Bagram airfield after preparations are completed.

Gromyko, Andropov, Ustinov and Ponomarev submit a top-secret report to the CC CPSU on the situation in Afghanistan, recommending sending an experienced general and officers, a parachute battalion to Bagram, a KGB detachment to Kabul and a GRU detachment to Bagram.
The CC CPSU Politburo approved the report's recommendations in Resolution No. P.156/XI, according to Liakhovskii.
actors: Communist Party of the Soviet Union

events.description: Proposed dispatch of a GRU special detachment to Bagram airfield after preparations are completed, for the protection of important government installations.
Proposed dispatch of a KGB special detachment (125-150 men), disguised as Embassy service personnel, to Kabul to defend the Soviet Embassy.
Proposed dispatch of a parachute battalion to Bagram airfield with Afghan agreement to protect Soviet air squadrons, disguised as an aviation-technical maintenance team.

sources_cited: A.A. Liakhovskii, The Tragedy and Valour of the Afghani (Moscow: GPI Iskon, 1995), p. 76
key_claims: Soviet leaders attributed DRA difficulties to economic backwardness, a small working class and PDPA weakness, worsened by lack of collegial leadership.
Power was concentrated in Taraki and Amin, who made mistakes and violated legality.
The army was the main support of the DRA government against counter-revolution, with security forces, border troops and self-defense forces taking more active roles.
Broad population strata were insufficiently involved against 'reaction', making government stabilization measures ineffective.
The Soviet MFA, KGB, Defense Ministry and International Department recommended sending a general and officers, a parachute battalion to Bagram, and KGB and GRU special detachments.
The Politburo approved these recommendations on 28 June 1979.
